_readme: Single source for every number published on any site, README, repo description or
archival record.
Rules:
1. No number appears on any public surface unless it has an id here.
2. produced_by must be a command that can be RUN. If it cannot, status is 'unbacked'
and the number may not appear in a headline, tagline or stat tile.
3. status 'withdrawn' means the number is retired. It must appear nowhere.
4. A ratio must carry its baseline in 'scope'. A ratio without a named baseline is unbacked.
5. Changing a value means re-running produced_by, not editing this file by hand.
6. A 'caveat' is part of the value and travels with it. 'note' is for whoever
maintains this file; 'caveat' is for whoever reads the number in public.
A single-run or provisional fact MUST have one, and build-sites.mjs refuses
to render it bare — the source must write {{fact:id+caveat}}. On a protocol
fact a caveat is optional context, because caveating everything teaches
readers to skip caveats.
7. Default to zero numbers. Tallies and measurements fail differently. A TALLY counts
things that grow — tests, files, runs, devices — and is stale the next commit; it may
only appear on the surface that generates it. A MEASUREMENT is frozen once made
(dated, machine-named, protocol) and may be republished, but only where it is
load-bearing: the claim that surface exists to make. Crosslink cards, footers,
taglines, nav links and repo descriptions are decorative surfaces — zero numbers
there. A sentence without a number cannot go stale. kind: 'tally' marks a count of
something that grows. Rule 7 machine form: the build refuses a tally in any headline
context, protocol or not.
8. Every fact with a runnable produced_by and a value must declare a 'cost': 'cheap'
(seconds, no GPU, no model download) or 'expensive' (a GPU bench, or a suite that
runs for minutes). check-facts.mjs --verify-cheap re-runs every cheap one on the
weekly sweep and REPORTS disagreement as FACT-DRIFT; it never writes here, because
rule 5 says a value changes by re-running produced_by, not by a script deciding it
should. Cost is measured, not guessed: one test-count fact touches no GPU and still
takes 9m30s, so it is expensive. zerotvm.wgsl_files drifted 50->51 and was caught
only because an agent happened to re-run it by hand; that is the gap this closes.
Entry shape:
id                  namespaced, project.quantity. Referenced as {{fact:id}} by the render gate.
value               number, or null when the quantity is registered but unmeasured.
unit                free text. 'x' and '%' additionally trigger the baseline check (rule 4).
scope               what was measured, on what, against what. Required.
produced_by         the command that regenerates the value, or a string starting UNRESOLVED.
cost                'cheap' | 'expensive'. Required when produced_by is runnable and value is set.
status              'protocol' | 'single-run' | 'provisional' | 'unbacked' | 'withdrawn'.
measured_at         ISO date.
measured_on         machine or environment string. Required for 'single-run'.
runs                array of raw observations behind a median, when a protocol round produced them.
runs_spread         string form of the same, when the raw array was not kept.
kind                'tally' when the quantity grows with the work. Barred from every headline surface.
caveat              the qualification a reader needs. Travels with the value to the surface.
note                maintenance context. Never rendered.
derived_from        ids this value is computed from. Checked to exist.
drift_tolerance_pct per-fact band for --verify-cheap. Only for values read from a live counter.
This file is the author's own registry, trimmed to the entries that show each shape.
The numbers are real and published. So are the notes, including the ones recording
where a wrong number was still live at the time of writing — that is what the
registry is for.
A produced_by below that points at the author's own checkouts will not run on your
machine. --verify-cheap reports those as UNREACHABLE, which is the correct answer:
UNREACHABLE is never agreement. 'example.lens_files' is repo-local and re-runs
green anywhere, so the pass has something real to exercise. produced_by commands
run from the repository root.

facts.scope: Phi-3-mini, total wall-clock decode, Apple M2 Max, same-session paired against WebLLM, 128 tokens, median of 5
facts.produced_by: cd ~/dev/zero-tvm && npm run bench && jq -r .ztDecode bench/results.json
facts.note: The protocol shape: a median with the raw runs kept beside it. A single number with no runs[] and no measured_on is a memory, not a measurement.

facts.scope: WebLLM baseline, identical weights, same session as zerotvm.phi3.decode_toks
facts.produced_by: cd ~/dev/zero-tvm && npm run bench && jq -r .webllmDecode bench/results.json

facts.scope: zerotvm.phi3.decode_toks over zerotvm.phi3.webllm_decode_toks, same session. AHEAD, not behind.
facts.note: The incident that started the registry. Two live sites published '22% behind WebLLM' for this quantity, from a baked copy of a generated file that nothing regenerated. The sign was inverted on a public surface for weeks. A derived fact names its inputs so the arithmetic can be re-run rather than remembered.

facts.scope: hand-written .wgsl files in src/compiler/shaders, excluding generated int4-matmul variants
facts.note: Five different counts were published at once: 18, 27, 42 and 55, plus this one. Only this one is produced by running something. It then moved 50->51 within a day of being corrected, which is why kind:'tally' exists — chasing a growing count buys one day and leaves the trap armed.

facts.scope: rows in the benchmark_runs table, all workloads
facts.caveat: read from a live, mutable table; a point-in-time count
facts.note: The repo README published 890 for this. That overstates by 96. drift_tolerance_pct 10: a dated snapshot of a live counter, so verify-cheap stays quiet within 10% and fires beyond it, when the published snapshot has become misleadingly stale. The tolerance is per-fact and declared, never global.

facts.scope: median single-kernel fusion speedup on Apple Silicon. Baseline NOT RECORDED HERE - must be named before republishing.
facts.produced_by: UNRESOLVED - published on a live site, query not recorded
facts.note: The live site published 71x / 56x / 20x as medians, and 226x / 402x / 103x elsewhere on the same page without stating which aggregate. Rule 4 applies: a ratio without a named baseline is unbacked, and unbacked may not sit in a headline, tagline or stat tile.

Superseded by the medians now on the live site. Survived in a stale baked copy of the generated file, and on one page as '2,865x' — comma-formatted, which a bare grep for 2865 never matched. That is why the withdrawn sweep generates thousands-separated variants. Must appear nowhere.

facts.scope: lens definitions in lenses/ in this repository, counted on disk from the repository root
facts.note: Repo-local so --verify-cheap has a fact it can actually re-run anywhere. It is a tally, so the render gate refuses it in a stat tile or tagline even though its status is protocol — the demonstration of rule 7's machine form.
